title: Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE
subtitle: An idol agency guards another Tokyo
summary: Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE is Atlus's Wii U role-playing game, first released in Japan on 26 December 2015.
body: Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE is Atlus's Wii U role-playing game, first released in Japan on 26 December 2015. Young performers at Fortuna Entertainment confront hostile Mirages that harvest human creative energy. Friendly Mirages drawn from Fire Emblem become their partners, letting the cast move between modern Tokyo and the dangerous Idolaspheres. Shibuya, Harajuku and the entertainment agency provide the everyday setting, while stage performance and supernatural combat become connected expressions of the same characters' growing confidence and abilities.

The turn-based battles build around weaknesses and Sessions, in which a successful attack leads allies into a chain of further actions. Choosing the right opening can therefore involve much more than the damage dealt by the first character. The player explores the Idolaspheres for resources and equipment while developing those linked abilities. Outside battle, the Wii U GamePad presents messages through the Topic app and supplies area maps. Communication among the cast remains visible alongside the journey through their ordinary work and their otherworldly responsibilities.

Nintendo proposed a crossover between Fire Emblem and Shin Megami Tensei, and Atlus shaped the collaboration into an original story about performers. Avex produced the musical numbers, with Yoshiaki Fujisawa composing the score. Side stories follow the ambitions of playable and supporting characters, tying their development to the entertainment setting. The Western edition arrived in June 2016 with Japanese voices and subtitles; an enhanced Switch version, Encore, followed in 2020. The original Wii U adventure makes the crossover's influences part of a new world rather than a simple meeting of existing casts.
